safeOrderingApplied: validate temp path differs from tracked original -> register in owned tempFiles[]/tempFilesCreated[] registry -> attempt write inside try/catch -> on write failure: unlink exact path (best-effort) + rethrow -> caller (runScenario/mutateFn) propagates -> outer runEntry() finally always runs cleanup regardless of where the throw occurred

throwBeforeWrite.description: Covered -- registration happens before fs.writeFileSync, so even a throw from writeFileSync itself is safe (file, if partially created, gets unlinked in the local catch; path is already in registry so outer finally would catch it too as a backstop).

partialWriteThenThrow.description: Covered -- same mechanism; the local try/catch around fs.writeFileSync unlinks whatever partial bytes exist before rethrowing.

writeSuccessRequireEvalThrow.description: Covered -- path already registered before write; require()/eval() failures happen after writeFileSync returns successfully, so the registered path is cleaned by the outer finally.

success.description: Covered -- normal path cleanup via cleanupTempFiles() (mutations.js, called at main() tail, ALSO idempotently re-run in runEntry() finally) or the runEntry() finally forEach (map-state-mutations.js).

cleanupOnAlreadyMissingFile.description: Covered -- both cleanup loops wrap each fs.unlinkSync in try/catch, silently continuing if the file is already gone.

tmpDirOwnership.mechanism: path.join(os.tmpdir(), ) -- unique per process id, not a fixed shared directory
tmpDirOwnership.note: Previously created at module top-level (before any try/finally existed). Moved inside runEntry()'s try block, immediately before bootstrapChildDb(), so its creation now lives within the same protected try/finally as bootstrap and main() -- a throw during or after its creation is guaranteed to reach the finally cleanup, not just the process.on("exit") fallback.
tmpDirOwnership.currentlyUnusedNote: TMP_DIR is not currently written into by any code path in this file (writeTempCopy() writes adjacent to originals instead) -- kept reserved/cleaned defensively, not dead-code-removed, since removing it was out of scope for this safety pass.

cleanupOwnershipVerification.trackedSourceNeverInRegistry: Verified: writeAdjacent()/writeTempCopy() both throw a [SAFETY] error if the computed temp path resolves equal to the tracked original path, before any registration or write occurs.

primaryErrorPreservation.problem: A throw inside a finally block replaces/masks any pending exception from the try block (JS semantics) -- if dbContext.cleanup() itself throws, it would silently discard the real test failure that caused main() to throw in the first place.
primaryErrorPreservation.fix: dbContext.cleanup() is now wrapped in its own try/catch inside the finally block in BOTH files; a cleanup failure is logged via console.error but never rethrown, so it cannot override a primary error from main(). The tempFiles/tempFilesCreated forEach loops already had per-file try/catch from the start (unaffected by this change).

processExitFallbackIdempotency.noDoubleLogOutput: fs.rmSync(..., { recursive: true, force: true }) does not throw or log when the target is already gone -- confirmed by force:true semantics -- so the process.on("exit") second-layer fallback produces no duplicate output whether or not the finally-based primary cleanup already ran.
